limits: Low granarycore is scored from Muse Spark 1.3 alone: Grok 4.6's primary review has no valid response (both attempts quoted code the submission does not contain), so the summary uses Muse's reviewed score and intent recovery for that run, as the frozen protocol does for any submission without two valid reviews. Every other run is the equal mean of both judges.
Muse Spark 1.3 passed calibration with the one-gate allowance: repeatability (g11) fell 0.1 short, within the half-point the protocol allows for one gate.

Grok 4.6's calibration stopped on a Cursor usage limit (the signed-in account was on the free plan) and resumed on the same call after the owner signed in to the paid account; the stopped attempts are archived, not counted.
The ChatGPT login reported plan prolite; earlier GPT columns ran on ChatGPT Pro. The plan sets usage limits, not the model served.
Model identity is requested-only: Codex does not report the serving model.
The sweep ran on release day and the day after, through Codex CLI 0.166.0 pinned by version; it cannot pin what OpenAI serves under the model id.
Frontier Code quality is the reviewed layer plus intent recovery and is never compared with Routine v1 Code quality.
One attempt per task and level, on the owner's Mac, local sandbox, flat 3-hour task bound, one task at a time.
publication_scope: Per-run scores, per-panel sub-scores, aggregates, judge protocol text, calibration verdicts and control means, integrity-audit verdicts, raw tokens and API-equivalent cost estimates.
withheld: quirk answer keys (they describe hidden-test behaviour)
reviewer session identifiers and usage receipts
integrity_limit: Hash checks bind the export to frozen files; they do not prove that judges were unbiased or that no training overlap exists.
